Round
ROWND
adj.
Webster 1828 treats ROUND as adjective: cylindrical, circular, spherical; full; smooth-flowing; plain / candid; brisk; plump. As noun: a circle; action in a circle; rotation in office; the step of a ladder; a watch performed about a garrison; a discharge of fire-arms. As adverb / preposition: on all sides; about (Luke 19:43, compass thee round). As verb: to make circular; to surround. This page fills the KJV-gap of what encircles. Companion pages already treat mountain, angel, and jerusalem.

Biblical Definition

Round in Scripture is not a meeting and not a brand of completeness. It names what encircles a people, for shelter or for siege. The wilderness will not let bread be a theory: there lay a small round thing, as small as the hoar frost on the ground (Exo 16:14). The psalmist will not let fear stand unguarded: The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them (Psa 34:7). Geography preaches: As the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so the LORD is round about his people (Psa 125:2). Zechariah will not let the unwalled city panic: I, saith the LORD, will be unto her a wall of fire round about (Zec 2:5). Luke will not let the same word stay only comfort: enemies compass thee round (Luk 19:43). The dictionary therefore keeps round from becoming either a committee or a charm. It is the Bible’s way of saying: around you — either the LORD, or the trench.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines ROUND as circular or spherical; full; candid. Noun: a circle; a course returning to its start; a watch about a garrison. Adverb/preposition: on all sides; about (Luke 19:43). Verb: to make circular; to surround.

expand to see more

ROUND, adjective 1. Cylindrical; circular; spherical or globular.

2. Full; large; as a round sum or price.

4. Plain; open; candid; fair. ROUND dealing is the honor of man's nature.

ROUND, noun A circle; a circular thing; action or performance in a circle; rotation in office; a rundle; the step of a ladder; a walk performed by a guard round a garrison.

ROUND, adverb 1. On all sides. Thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round. Luke 19:43.

ROUND, preposition On every side of; as, the people stood round him.

ROUND, verb transitive To make circular, spherical or cylindrical; to surround; to encircle; to encompass.

Key Scripture

Exo 16:14 — "And when the dew that lay was gone up, behold, upon the face of the wilderness there lay a small round thing, as small as the hoar frost on the ground."

Psa 34:7 — "The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them."

Psa 125:2 — "As the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so the LORD is round about his people from henceforth even for ever."

Zec 2:5 — "For I, saith the LORD, will be unto her a wall of fire round about, and will be the glory in the midst of her."

Luk 19:43 — "For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side,"

Modern Corruption

Round is corrupted when the LORD-round-about is recast as a support circle, when manna’s small round thing is treated as a lifestyle snack, and when Luke 19’s compass-round is ignored so that encircling always means safety.

expand to see more

The first corruption is Psalm 34 as a group. The angel of the LORD encamps round about them that fear him. Fear of the LORD, not a facilitated circle, is the condition. The recovery is a holy encampment, not a roundtable.

The second corruption is Exodus 16 as branding. The small round thing is manna, bread from heaven, measured and for the day. It is not artisan completeness. Hunger is answered by the LORD, not by shape.

The third corruption is one-sided encircling. Psalm 125 and Zechariah 2 are the LORD round about as mountains and fire. Luke 19:43 is enemies who compass thee round. The same geometry can be siege. Comfort without that verse is a lie.

Psalm 34:7, Psalm 125:2, and Zechariah 2:5 are KJV-verified; no Strong’s tag on round in this cache.

Usage

"Manna lay a small round thing on the wilderness (Exo 16:14)."

"The angel encamps round about them that fear (Psa 34:7); mountains and the LORD are round about His people (Psa 125:2)."

"The LORD is a wall of fire round about (Zec 2:5); enemies also compass round (Luk 19:43)."
